_doc: Category 16 (Dietary Supplements, human) compiler config for compile-cat16.mjs. THE DECIDED METHOD (Karen's call): every (subcategory, analyte) is set to the strictest sovereign INFANT-AND-CHILD-FOOD maximum level (HMTc Category 1, Ages 0-5), read across to ALL supplements regardless of adult or child labeling, as a voluntary child-protective over-compliance. Rationale: children routinely consume adult supplements (gummies, protein, greens, melatonin) and body-weight-normalized exposure makes the child the binding safety case. Every value is a `read_across` with child_protective:true, never `gov` — no government sets an infant-food limit for an adult supplement; HMTc adopts the child limit by choice, and that honesty is the defensibility. The laxer adult floor (sovereign adult food-supplement MLs, USP <2232> oral PDE, Prop 65 developmental MADL) is disclosed on every cell via adult_floor and NEVER selects the number. The clay/mineral/earth and greens/superfood classes (Pb/As/Cd hyperaccumulators) get the SAME strict numbers — the compiler never relaxes a limit for a high-occurrence class; hazard_note records why the line is held. The anchor is a fixed curated register-sourced infant-food ML applied uniformly; no occurrence statistic, no invented value, and no serving-size conversion selects a limit.
lineage: Cat 16 v1.0 (2026-08-13). HMTc Method v2.0, child-protective over-compliance form. Method forked from compile-cat17.mjs (human-grade over-compliance) and ported to the self-contained compile-cat27.mjs derive->audit->verify shape. Infant-food anchors are the strictest sovereign infant/child-food MLs on the register as of 2026-08-13.
audit_scope: infant|baby food|young child|young-child|toddler|complementary|follow-on|follow-up|weaning|porridge|cereal-based|processed cereal|formula food|milk substitute|foods for infants
audit_exclude: supplement|health supplement|dietary supplement|traditional medicine|\btoy|paint|cosmetic|jewel|crayon|surface coat|migration|children.s product|consumer product
regulatory_floor_note: Dietary supplements are legally governed by an adult-oriented framework: FDA DSHEA sets no heavy-metal maxima; USP <2232> computes elemental-contaminant PDEs for an adult consumer; the food-supplement maximum levels several governments set (EU, GSO, Israel, Vietnam, Thailand, ASEAN, Singapore) are lax (lead 1000-10000, cadmium 300-1000, mercury 100-500 ug/kg). HMTc holds every supplement, adult- or child-labeled, to the strictest sovereign infant-and-child-food maximum level (Ages 0-5) by choice. The adult floor is disclosed on every cell and never selects the number.
usp_2232_citation: USP General Chapter <2232> Elemental Contaminants in Dietary Supplements. Oral permitted daily exposure (PDE), µg/day. USP Option 2 assumes a maximum daily intake of 10 g of the supplement, so the concentration equivalent is PDE / 0.01 kg = PDE x 100 µg/kg. USP <2232> covers only lead, cadmium, inorganic arsenic, and mercury (total and methyl); it sets no limit for nickel, tin, aluminium, or chromium.
prop65_citation: California Proposition 65 (OEHHA) Maximum Allowable Dose Levels — safe-harbour warning triggers in µg/day, not food maximum levels. Lead oral MADL 0.5 µg/day (reproductive/developmental endpoint); cadmium oral MADL 4.1 µg/day (developmental); hexavalent chromium oral MADL 8.2 µg/day. OEHHA has adopted no oral safe-harbour for inorganic arsenic or nickel. Values consistent with the cert briefing 'Named as a Hazard, Left Unlimited' (the-prop-65-gap).

Pb.analog_label: AU-NZ Standard 1.4.1 infant-formula lead maximum (the strictest sovereign infant lead ML)
Pb.label: Child-protective read-across from the strictest sovereign infant-and-child-food lead maximum (AU-NZ infant formula, 10 µg/kg). Adult supplement floors run 1000-10000 µg/kg (Thailand 1000; GSO/Israel/Vietnam 3000; ASEAN/Singapore 10000) and adult USP <2232> permits 5 µg/day (500 µg/kg at 10 g/day); California's developmental lead MADL is 0.5 µg/day. HMTc holds ALL supplements to 10 µg/kg because children consume adult supplements and lead has no threshold.

Cd.analog_label: EU 2023/915 infant-formula cadmium maximum (the strictest sovereign infant cadmium ML)
Cd.label: Child-protective read-across from the strictest sovereign infant-and-child-food cadmium maximum (EU infant formula, 5 µg/kg). Adult supplement floors run 300-1000 µg/kg; adult USP <2232> permits 5 µg/day (500 µg/kg at 10 g/day); California's developmental cadmium MADL is 4.1 µg/day. HMTc holds ALL supplements to 5 µg/kg.

tAs.analog_label: India FSSAI infant-food total-arsenic maximum (the strictest sovereign infant total-arsenic ML)
tAs.label: Child-protective read-across from the strictest sovereign infant-and-child-food total-arsenic maximum (India infant foods, 50 µg/kg). Total arsenic gates the inorganic-arsenic reflex; the toxic species iAs is anchored separately at 10 µg/kg. Adult supplement floors run 300-5000 µg/kg. HMTc holds ALL supplements to 50 µg/kg total arsenic.

iAs.analog_label: EU 2023/915 infant-formula inorganic-arsenic maximum (the strictest sovereign infant iAs ML)
iAs.label: Child-protective read-across from the strictest sovereign infant-and-child-food inorganic-arsenic maximum (EU infant formula, 10 µg/kg). No government sets an inorganic-arsenic supplement ML; adult USP <2232> permits inorganic arsenic 15 µg/day (1500 µg/kg at 10 g/day). HMTc holds ALL supplements to 10 µg/kg inorganic arsenic — 150x below the adult USP concentration floor.

tHg.analog_label: Israel FCS-2016 infant/toddler-formula total-mercury maximum (the strictest sovereign infant total-mercury ML)
tHg.label: Child-protective read-across from the strictest sovereign infant-and-child-food total-mercury maximum (Israel infant/toddler formula ready-to-eat, 4 µg/kg). Adult supplement floors run 100-500 µg/kg; adult USP <2232> permits total mercury 15 µg/day (1500 µg/kg at 10 g/day). HMTc holds ALL supplements to 4 µg/kg.

Ni.analog_label: EU 2024/1987 liquid infant/young-child-formula nickel maximum (the strictest sovereign infant nickel ML)
Ni.label: Child-protective read-across from the strictest sovereign infant-and-child-food nickel maximum (EU liquid infant/young-child formula, 100 µg/kg). No government sets a nickel supplement ML and adult USP <2232> sets none; the entire adult framework is silent on supplement nickel, a metal EFSA reports European diets already exceed the tolerable intake for, children most of all. HMTc holds ALL supplements to 100 µg/kg.

Sn.analog_label: India FSSAI infant-food tin maximum (the only non-canned infant tin ML on the register)
Sn.label: Child-protective read-across from the India FSSAI non-canned infant-food tin maximum (5000 µg/kg). Tin is a can-migration analyte; a non-canned supplement has no intrinsic tin source, so any quantifiable tin triggers a packaging investigation. No adult supplement tin ML exists. HMTc holds ALL supplements to 5000 µg/kg.

Al.analog_label: AU-NZ Standard 1.4.1 non-soy infant-formula aluminium maximum (the only sovereign food aluminium ML on the register)
Al.label: Child-protective read-across from the AU-NZ non-soy infant-formula aluminium maximum (500 µg/kg) — the only government aluminium ML for any food in any jurisdiction. No adult supplement aluminium ML exists and USP <2232> sets none. HMTc holds ALL supplements to 500 µg/kg.

Cr.control: No government sets a total-chromium maximum level for any infant-and-child food, so no child-protective numeric anchor exists and none is invented. Total chromium is measured on every lot as a mandatory surveillance control and gates the hexavalent-chromium reflex. Cr(III) is nutritionally essential; the toxic species is Cr(VI), controlled separately. No adult supplement total-chromium ML exists.
Cr.reference_method: Total Cr by ICP-MS after microwave acid digestion.

Cr-VI.control: Hexavalent chromium reduces to Cr(III) in a reducing supplement matrix and carries no stable burden; it is bounded by total chromium, measured on every lot. Any total-Cr result at or above 100 µg/kg triggers Cr(VI) speciation, and any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails certification. California lists Cr(VI) under Proposition 65 (oral MADL 8.2 µg/day) but sets no food concentration limit.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total Cr by ICP-MS; Cr(VI) by EPA 3060A alkaline extraction with IC-ICP-MS (EPA 6800 / EN 15192) on a total-Cr exceedance; LOQ-level quantifiable Cr(VI) = fail.

MeHg.control: Total mercury is measured on every lot and bounds the methylmercury fraction (MeHg <= tHg). Reflex methylmercury speciation is required when the formulation contains marine-derived ingredients (fish, algae, seaweed, marine collagen, marine oil) or when total mercury approaches the child-protective ceiling. No government sets a supplement methylmercury limit below the binding total-mercury read-across.
MeHg.reference_method: Total Hg by EPA 7473 or ICP-MS; MeHg by species-specific GC-ICP-MS / HPLC-ICP-MS on marine-containing or elevated-tHg lots.

MeHg.control: This class carries a credible methylmercury methylation and biomagnification pathway (marine algae, seaweed, fish oil, marine-derived material). Methylmercury is measured on every lot by species-specific speciation, not only reflexively, and is bounded by the child-protective total-mercury ceiling; any methylmercury above the bounding total-mercury result triggers investigation and any exceedance of the total-mercury ceiling fails.
MeHg.reference_method: Total Hg by EPA 7473 or ICP-MS on every lot; MeHg by species-specific GC-ICP-MS / HPLC-ICP-MS on every lot of this class.

MeHg.control: This class carries a credible methylmercury methylation and biomagnification pathway (marine oil, marine-derived material). Methylmercury is measured on every lot by species-specific speciation, not only reflexively, and is bounded by the child-protective total-mercury ceiling.
MeHg.reference_method: Total Hg by EPA 7473 or ICP-MS on every lot; MeHg by species-specific GC-ICP-MS / HPLC-ICP-MS on every lot of this class.

supplements-oral-solids-gummies.name: Oral solids: gummies/chewables
supplements-oral-solids-gummies.hazard_note: Gummies and chewables are the supplement form most likely to be consumed by children directly (candy-like presentation); the child-protective limit is therefore not a read-across for this form but the literal binding case.

supplements-oral-solids-powders.name: Oral solids: powders (bulk tubs, sachets, stick packs)

supplements-oral-liquids-syrups.name: Oral liquids: syrups
supplements-oral-liquids-syrups.hazard_note: Pediatric syrups (children's multivitamin/mineral, iron, elderberry) are formulated and marketed for children; the child-protective limit is the literal binding case, not a read-across.

supplements-oral-liquids-droppers.name: Oral liquids: droppers
supplements-oral-liquids-droppers.hazard_note: Dropper-dosed liquids (infant vitamin D, probiotic drops) are dosed directly to infants and young children; the child-protective limit is the literal binding case.

supplements-teas-labeled.name: Food-like forms: teas (when labeled as supplement)
supplements-teas-labeled.hazard_note: Botanical tea material can hyperaccumulate lead, cadmium, and arsenic from soil; the child-protective limit is held on the dry material and never relaxed for occurrence.

supplements-bars-labeled.name: Food-like forms: bars (when labeled as supplement)

supplements-vitamin-mineral.name: Ingredient class — vitamin/mineral (single, multi-mineral, multi-vitamin/mineral)
supplements-vitamin-mineral.hazard_note: Mineral raw materials (calcium, magnesium, trace-mineral concentrates) are a recognised lead and cadmium source; the child-protective limit is held on the finished product and never relaxed for occurrence.

supplements-botanicals-herbs.name: Ingredient class — botanicals/herbs/traditional formulas
supplements-botanicals-herbs.hazard_note: Botanicals and traditional herbal formulas are a documented lead and arsenic source (soil uptake, some Ayurvedic and traditional preparations intentionally metal-containing); the child-protective limit is held and never relaxed for occurrence.

supplements-algae-seaweed-based.name: Ingredient class — algae/seaweed-based
supplements-algae-seaweed-based.hazard_note: Algae and seaweed hyperaccumulate cadmium and inorganic arsenic and carry a credible marine methylmercury pathway; the child-protective limits are held and never relaxed for occurrence, and methylmercury is measured on every lot.

supplements-protein-collagen-powders.name: Ingredient class — protein/collagen powders
supplements-protein-collagen-powders.hazard_note: Plant-protein isolates (rice, pea) can carry inorganic arsenic and cadmium; marine collagen carries a methylmercury pathway (covered by the mercury reflex control). The child-protective limit is held and never relaxed for occurrence.

supplements-oil-based.name: Ingredient class — oil-based supplements (fish oil/omega-3 and similar)
supplements-oil-based.hazard_note: Fish-oil and marine-oil supplements carry a credible methylmercury pathway; methylmercury is measured on every lot. The child-protective limits are held and never relaxed for occurrence.

supplements-clay-mineral-earth.name: Ingredient class — clay/mineral/earth-derived (bentonite, diatomaceous earth, zeolite, shilajit)
supplements-clay-mineral-earth.hazard_note: Geologic materials (bentonite, diatomaceous earth, zeolite, shilajit) are the highest lead- and arsenic-occurrence class in the category — shilajit in particular routinely carries lead and arsenic far above every child-food limit. The child-protective limits are held at full strictness and NEVER relaxed for occurrence; this class is where the over-compliance bites hardest and the adult framework is effectively silent.

supplements-mushroom-fungal.name: Ingredient class — mushroom/fungal extracts (lion's mane, reishi, cordyceps, chaga)
supplements-mushroom-fungal.hazard_note: Fungi hyperaccumulate cadmium and mercury from substrate (chaga and reishi in particular); the child-protective limits are held and never relaxed for occurrence, and the mercury reflex control applies.

supplements-greens-superfood.name: Ingredient class — greens/superfood blends
supplements-greens-superfood.hazard_note: Greens and superfood blends combine leaf, root, algae, and cereal-grass material that hyperaccumulate lead, cadmium, and inorganic arsenic; the child-protective limits are held at full strictness and NEVER relaxed for occurrence. Blends containing algae/seaweed also carry the marine methylmercury reflex.
